qpr_core_00.title: Game marginals, the winning effect, and the scaffolding for convex mixtures of strategies
qpr_core_00.nl: This bundle opens the development with a handful of elementary quantities attached to a game and a strategy, followed by the raw material for combining strategies convexly. The two marginals of the question distribution are $\mu_A(x) = \sum_y \mu(x,y)$ and $\mu_B(y) = \sum_x \mu(x,y)$; `quadraticExpectation` is the real quadratic form $z \mapsto \mathrm{Re}\,\langle z, W z\rangle$ of a bounded operator; and the *winning effect* at a question pair $(x,y)$ is the positive operator $\sum_{a,b} [V(x,y,a,b)]\, A^x_a \otimes B^y_b$, obtained by summing the joint measurement operators over the answer pairs the verifier accepts, so that the winning probability at $(x,y)$ is the Born trace of the state against it. The remaining declarations set up a mixture of a finite family of strategies $(S_j)_{j \in J}$: the local systems $\bigsqcup_j \mathcal{A}_j$ and $\bigsqcup_j \mathcal{B}_j$, the "matched" index set $\bigsqcup_j (\mathcal{A}_j \times \mathcal{B}_j)$ that records both labels with a *common* flag $j$, the diagonal inclusion of the matched set into the product of the two disjoint unions, the $0/1$ matrix implementing that inclusion, and the block-diagonal matrix $\bigoplus_j p_j \rho_j$. These last pieces are assembled into an actual strategy in the next bundle.

qpr_core_01.title: Convex mixtures, pure and flagged strategies, finite event laws, and the spectral filter calculus
qpr_core_01.nl: Cut by dependency order, this bundle is thematically mixed; it contains four groups. First, the mixture construction is completed: conjugating the block-diagonal matrix $\bigoplus_j p_j \rho_j$ by the matched-index embedding gives a density matrix on the two disjoint unions, the players' POVMs are taken block-diagonal, and `convexMixtureStrategy` is the resulting single strategy, whose winning probability is the $p$-average of the winning probabilities of the $S_j$. Second, pure strategies: the rank-one density matrix $|z\rangle\langle z|$ of a unit vector, the strategy determined by a unit vector on $\mathbb{C}^{d_A} \otimes \mathbb{C}^{d_B}$ together with POVM families for each question, and a *flagged* variant carrying an extra classical register $J$. Third, a small probability layer: `FiniteEventLaw` is a nonnegative weight summing to $1$ on a finite sample space, with the mass of an event, the event $\{\omega : \text{all coordinates } i \in D \text{ win}\}$, and the failure mass $\mathrm{mass}(\text{win } D) - \mathrm{mass}(\text{win } D \cup \{i\})$; specialising to outcomes $(x,y,a,b)$ with weight $\mu(x,y)\Pr[a,b \mid x,y]$ gives the event law of a strategy, and `repeatedCoordinateWin` reads off whether coordinate $i$ of a repeated outcome is accepted. Fourth, a spectral functional calculus for positive semidefinite matrices: conjugation by the eigenvector unitary as a real-linear continuous map, $f$ applied to the eigenvalues (giving the support inverse, the support projection and the square root), the resolvent filters $\lambda/(\lambda+s)$ and their squares, the real bilinear Born pairing $(F,G) \mapsto \mathrm{Re}\,\mathrm{tr}(\rho\,(F \otimes G))$, the conditional question distributions $\mu(y \mid x)$ and $\mu(x \mid y)$ with the averages they induce, the operators obtained from a repeated strategy by conditioning on answers on a subset $D$, and a refinement of a POVM through a purification map $\Gamma$ with $\Gamma^\dagger\Gamma = F$, where the leftover $1 - \Gamma F^{-1} \Gamma^\dagger$ is dumped on a distinguished outcome so that the refinement is again a POVM.

qpr_core_02.title: Subset histories, spectral entropy kernels, and the embezzlement/Schmidt toolkit
qpr_core_02.nl: Three largely independent strands sit in this bundle. The first is the *subset history*: for disjoint sets of coordinates $D$ (conditioned) and $L$ (revealed to Alice), a `FullSubsetHistory` records both players' questions on $D$, Alice's questions on $L$, and Bob's questions on the remaining coordinates; around it are the maps reassembling a history plus hidden questions into full question tuples, the bijection repackaging (history, hidden Alice questions, hidden Bob questions) as an ordinary pair of question tuples, the product weight of a history under $\mu^{\otimes n}$, the conditional weights of the hidden coordinates, the Alice and Bob *filters* obtained by averaging the strategy's conditioned operators over the hidden questions, and the win indicators for the conditioned coordinates. The second strand is second-order spectral data: the entropy kernel with eigenvalues $\lambda/(1+s) - \lambda/(\lambda+s)$ and its diagonal form, weighted variance and Jensen-type combinations across a family of positive semidefinite matrices, the rank-one spectral atoms (eigenprojections) of such a matrix, the Born weight of an atom against a partner operator, and an entropy potential summing these over all histories. The third strand is a toolkit of bipartite states and unitaries: the van Dam--Hayden embezzling state with diagonal amplitudes $(j+1)^{-1/2}$ normalized by the harmonic number, maximally entangled states, diagonal Schmidt states and general Schmidt vectors produced by local unitaries, permutation and entrywise-conjugate unitaries, tensor products of vectors indexed by a finite set, a shared resource state weighted by a threshold profile $\tau$, the transpose of a POVM, and the Born probabilities of a pair of binary POVMs on a bipartite state, split into joint success, joint continuation, and mismatch — the accounting used later to track an accept/continue test performed by both players at once.

qpr_core_03.title: Catalyst unitaries, spectral partition POVMs, and uniform threshold grids
qpr_core_03.nl: This bundle collects small constructions that the rounding argument uses as building blocks. On the state side: the diagonal Schmidt state of a coefficient vector with $\sum_i \sigma_i^2 = 1$ packaged as a bipartite unit vector; the permutation unitary that sorts the amplitudes of a Schmidt vector tensored with an embezzling state into decreasing order, together with the scalar overlap term of that comparison; and the lift of a $d$-dimensional unitary to $\mathbb{C}^{dn}$ acting as $U \otimes 1$ under the standard bijection $\mathrm{Fin}\,d \times \mathrm{Fin}\,n \simeq \mathrm{Fin}\,(dn)$. On the measurement side, `coherentSharedRandomControlledUnitary` is the block-diagonal unitary $\bigoplus_\omega U_\omega$ controlled by a shared classical register, and `spectralPartitionPOVM` turns a binning of the eigenvalues of a positive semidefinite matrix into the projective POVM whose outcome $k$ is the sum of the eigenprojections in bin $k$. Finally, the threshold apparatus: an equally spaced grid of $N$ points in an interval, and the fraction of those grid points that lie between two reals $a$ and $b$ — a discretized $|a-b|$, which is how a continuous threshold test is replaced by a finite one. The last two definitions attach to a bipartite unit vector $\xi$ its coefficient matrix $M_\xi(b,a) = \xi(a,b)$ and the reduced density $M_\xi^\dagger M_\xi$ of one marginal.

qpr_core_04.title: Canonical Schmidt data and the first layer of the threshold-rounding apparatus
qpr_core_04.nl: The first two definitions read off the canonical Schmidt data of a bipartite unit vector: the coefficients are the square roots of the eigenvalues of its reduced density matrix, and a spectral energy pairs the atoms of two such reduced densities against each other. The remainder starts the `dSV`-prefixed sub-development, a self-contained rounding apparatus that converts a numerical threshold test into a quantum measurement. Its atoms are the *soft pass* function $x \mapsto x/(x+t)$, which compresses a spectral value into $[0,1)$; the other marginal $M_\xi M_\xi^\dagger$ of a target vector; the unnormalized diagonal vector supported on the first $r$ basis pairs, which truncates a state to a given rank; and a construction taking a family of projectors $P_k$ with $P_k$ and $1-P_k$ both positive semidefinite to a two-outcome POVM on the direct sum $\bigsqcup_k \mathbb{C}^d$, so that one of $k$ classical threshold choices is measured coherently. Also here are the survival product $\prod_{i<k} c_i$ of the first $k$ continuation probabilities, the local index type $\bigsqcup_{k \in \mathrm{Fin}\,N} \mathrm{Fin}\,d$ pairing a threshold register with a $d$-dimensional system, and the shared state on it built from the threshold resource with uniform weights.

qpr_core_05.title: Permutation-based correlated sampling and finite-alphabet information measures
qpr_core_05.nl: The bundle mixes three groups. It first finishes the shared threshold resource: the pure density matrix of the threshold state, $L$ independent copies with the linear isometry that reindexes a tensor of pairs into a pair of tensors, and two discrepancy functionals that compare the Schmidt spectra of two target vectors, one weighted by $|\sigma_i^2 - \tau_j^2|$ and one by $(\sigma_i + \tau_j)^2$, both against spectral-atom overlaps. It then gives a classical correlated-sampling gadget: with a uniformly random permutation of a finite set as shared randomness, `markedFirst` returns the marked element of least rank, and the fibers of that map, the uniform probability of a permutation event, and the normalized symmetric-difference distance between two marked sets record its behaviour; a rational distribution $p_i = \mathrm{num}_i/\mathrm{den}$ is realised as a marked subset of $\iota \times \mathrm{Fin}(\mathrm{den})$, so that two parties holding nearby rational distributions and the same permutation produce the same sample with high probability. The third group is elementary information theory over finite alphabets: relative entropy $\sum_i q_i \, \mathrm{klFun}(p_i/q_i)$ written through Mathlib's `klFun`, total variation $\tfrac12 \sum_i |p_i - q_i|$, the slack in the quadratic Pinsker-type lower bound $\mathrm{klFun}(x) \ge 3(x-1)^2/(2(x+2))$, the rounding of a distribution to a rational one with fixed denominator (floor numerators with the residual placed on a base point), and grouped masses, first marginals and conditionals of a joint distribution.

qpr_core_06.title: The uniform threshold grid and its mismatch functional
qpr_core_06.nl: Here the abstract grid of the earlier bundle is specialised: `dSVUniformDensityThresholdGrid` places $N$ equally spaced thresholds in $[1/N,\,1+1/N]$, each carrying weight $1/N$. Two functionals read a real number through this grid: the *prefix* is the total weight of thresholds lying below a given density, a discretization of the density itself, and the *mismatch* of two reals is the total weight of thresholds separating them, a discretization of their distance. Alongside these sit the conjugate-swap involution $\xi(i,j) \mapsto \overline{\xi(j,i)}$ on bipartite vectors, which exchanges the roles of the two marginals and so lets a statement proved for one side be transported to the other, together with the Schmidt coefficients and spectral discrepancy of the *left* reduced density, mirroring the right-hand versions defined earlier. The bundle closes with `normalizeOrDefault`, which normalizes a nonzero vector and returns a supplied fallback at $0$.

qpr_core_07.title: Rank-truncated unit targets and left Schmidt bases
qpr_core_07.nl: Three short definitions. The first produces, for each rank $r \le d$, a bipartite unit vector by normalizing the diagonal prefix vector supported on the first $r$ basis pairs, falling back to the embezzling state when that prefix is zero; this gives a family of maximally entangled states of prescribed rank, indexed uniformly by $r \in \mathrm{Fin}(d+1)$. The second is the eigenvector unitary of the left reduced density of a target vector, i.e. the local basis in which that marginal is diagonal. The third is the conjugate-swap map $v(i,j) \mapsto \overline{v(j,i)}$ at the level of raw vectors, the unnormalized form of the involution used to interchange the two marginals.

qpr_core_08.title: Conjugate-swapped targets and tensor-power local unitaries
qpr_core_08.nl: The first two definitions package the conjugate swap $\xi(i,j) \mapsto \overline{\xi(j,i)}$ as a map on bipartite *unit* vectors (the swap is norm preserving) and record the Schmidt coefficients of the left reduced density of a target, namely the square roots of its eigenvalues. The third is unrelated in content and enters only by dependency order: given a family $(U_i)_{i \in \iota}$ of unitaries on $\mathbb{C}^\beta$, it writes the entries of the tensor product $\bigotimes_i U_i$ as a matrix indexed by functions $\iota \to \beta$, via the product of entries $\prod_i (U_i)_{q(i)\,r(i)}$. That matrix is shown to be unitary in the next bundle.

qpr_core_09.title: Multi-copy history registers and the $L^2(0,\infty)$ purification space
qpr_core_09.nl: Three strands. The first turns the entrywise tensor product of local unitaries into an element of the unitary group on $\iota \to \beta$, and adds a version controlled by a shared classical register. The second builds the *whole-history* register of the multi-copy protocol: a stopping flag in $\mathrm{Fin}(L+1)$ together with $L+1$ copies of the threshold register, the shared state on it, an equivalence splitting that index into a $d$-dimensional target factor and a catalyst remainder, and the controlled unitaries with which Alice and Bob rotate every copy into the relevant local Schmidt basis. The third strand is analytic: the resolvent profile $s \mapsto z/(z+s)$ of a nonnegative real lies in $L^2\big((0,\infty)\big)$, so a family of positive semidefinite matrices $F_i$ together with a dominating $M$ generates a finite-dimensional subspace of that $L^2$ space — the *common purification subspace* — inside which all members of the family are simultaneously purified; matrix entries of the resolvent filter are likewise viewed as elements of the same $L^2$ space.

qpr_core_10.title: Finite-dimensional purification matrices and the purification of a strategy
qpr_core_10.nl: This bundle converts the analytic purification of the previous one into finite matrices and then applies it to a strategy. Selecting an orthonormal basis of the common purification subspace turns each ensemble member (and the ensemble mean) into an explicit rectangular matrix $\Gamma_a$ on $d \times \mathrm{Fin}(\dim)$ with $\Gamma_a^\dagger \Gamma_a = F_a$, so that a whole family of positive semidefinite matrices acquires purifications inside one common space. The second group purifies a strategy itself: the vectorization of a matrix as a vector on $d \times d$, a reindexing bijection $(\mathcal{A} \times (\mathcal{A}\times\mathcal{B})) \times \mathcal{B} \simeq (\mathcal{A}\times\mathcal{B}) \times (\mathcal{A}\times\mathcal{B})$, and the pure vector built from the square root of the strategy's shared state, whose reduced state on the original registers is that state. Finally, `purificationAlicePOVM` extends a POVM to the enlarged local system by tensoring with the identity on the added purifying register, which is what makes the purified system usable by a player who cannot touch the ancilla.

qpr_core_11.title: Purified strategies and projective threshold measurements
qpr_core_11.nl: The first three definitions record that one may assume the shared state of a strategy is pure: `purifiedStrategy` replaces a strategy by the pure-vector strategy on the enlarged local systems, with each player's POVM padded by the identity on their purifying register, and two auxiliary constructions build joint matrices and vectors from local maps $K_A$, $K_B$ applied to a strategy's state. The rest of the bundle installs the projective form of the threshold test: for a positive semidefinite $F$ and a grid index $k$, a binary bin tests whether the soft-pass value $\lambda/(\lambda+w)$ of an eigenvalue exceeds the $k$-th threshold, and the corresponding spectral partition POVM is a two-outcome *projective* measurement; specialising $F$ to the left reduced density of a bipartite target yields the accept projector at threshold $k$. Two error functionals compare two targets $\xi$, $\zeta$ through these projectors: an atom mismatch weighted by spectral-atom overlaps, and the accepted diagonal mass of a single target. Two further definitions here belong to the coherent stopped-state layer and appear only for dependency reasons.

qpr_core_12.title: Global threshold POVM and its Born success and cross-hazard functionals
qpr_core_12.nl: Four definitions built directly on the projective threshold test. Assembling the accept projectors across all $N$ grid points gives a single two-outcome POVM on the combined register $\bigsqcup_{k} \mathbb{C}^d$, in which the threshold is chosen by the shared classical register rather than by hand. Evaluating that POVM for Alice against its transpose for Bob on the shared threshold state gives the joint-success Born probability, the probability that both players accept at the same threshold. The cross-hazard functional measures instead the discrepancy between two targets, summing over thresholds the traces built from the differences $P_k(\xi) - P_k(\zeta)$ of their accept projectors. The last definition repeats the accept projector under a name used by the "complete" variant of the construction in the following bundle.

qpr_core_13.title: Canonical accepted target of the threshold test
qpr_core_13.nl: This bundle describes what the accepted branch of the threshold test is supposed to look like. The accept projectors are again assembled into a two-outcome POVM on the whole register, and `dSVDensityRationalCompleteProjectiveOutcome` gives the four unnormalized post-measurement vectors $(P_a \otimes Q_b)\,|\,\text{shared state}\rangle$ for the possible pairs of binary results, so that success, continuation and mismatch branches can be compared as vectors rather than only as probabilities. The canonical target is then the Schmidt vector whose $i$-th coefficient is $\sqrt{w \cdot \mathrm{prefix}_N\!\big(\lambda_i/(\lambda_i+w)\big)}$, expressed in an Alice basis obtained from a polar-decomposition existence statement, together with its normalization. Because the prefix is the grid discretization of the soft-pass value, this is exactly the state whose Schmidt spectrum is the target spectrum reweighted by the acceptance profile.

qpr_core_14.title: Sequential accept/stop dynamics, phase buckets, and coordinate-reveal histories
qpr_core_14.nl: This is the largest bundle and, being cut by dependency order, is genuinely mixed. Its main strand is the repeated form of the threshold protocol: $L$ copies of the test are performed in sequence, a stopping flag records the first accepting copy (via the accept set, the first-accepted index, and the permutation — realized as a unitary — that swaps that branch into a canonical position), Alice and Bob apply controlled local unitaries determined by their own targets, and the resulting physical state is analysed stage by stage: per-stage success, continuation and *asynchronous* masses (one player accepts, the other does not), the survival probability as a product of continuation probabilities, stopped success, stopped asynchronous and terminal masses, a per-stage hazard ratio, and a uniform escape rate $1/(2(W+1)d)$. A second strand coarsens ranks with public randomness: a logarithmic label $\lfloor Q \log r\rfloor$ shifted by a random phase is grouped into buckets with chosen representatives, giving phase-weighted crossing errors, in single-scale and multiscale versions, along with the index equivalences and isometries that reindex history, catalyst and harmonic registers into a single $\mathrm{Fin}(d \cdot \text{residual})$ factor of the form embezzlement arguments need. A third, short strand is uniform weights over Boolean bipartitions of a finite set — fair, reverse and marked variants — for averaging over a random split of the coordinates. Finally, back on the game side, the bundle defines entropy atoms (a subset history together with the conditioned answers of both players) with their counting weight and Born mass, and introduces `FullCoordinateRevealHistory`, a subset history with one distinguished coordinate $i$ held out, plus the bijections relating histories for $(D,L)$ and $(D, L \cup \{i\})$ and the associated Alice question filters.

qpr_core_15.title: Random orderings, forward seeds, and the exact reveal history
qpr_core_15.nl: The bundle first completes the one-coordinate reveal calculus: Bob's question filters, the assembly of hidden question tuples with the corresponding bijections, the per-coordinate entropy increment of a reveal history, and its total over all histories and conditioned answers. It then introduces the two models of *which* coordinates each player learns. The simpler one is a uniformly random permutation of the coordinates outside $D$, with the prefix of the first $k$ of them, and the average of a functional over permutation and position. The richer one is `ExactForwardSeed`: a distinguished coordinate, a Boolean bipartition of the remaining coordinates into an Alice (left) and a Bob (right) side, an ordering of each side, and a cut position on each side; its uniform weight is written explicitly and an equivalence to a $\Sigma$-tuple makes it a finite type. `ExactRevealHistory` is the history that goes with a seed — both players' questions and answers on $D$, Alice's questions on her prefix and Bob's on his — again with a tuple form and a finiteness instance. The remaining definitions attach analytic data to such a history: its prior mass under $\mu^{\otimes n}$, the induced Alice, Bob and joint question masses, the measurement filters obtained by summing the strategy's conditioned operators over question tuples compatible with the history (with mean and single-coordinate variants), and the families of positive semidefinite matrices to be fed to the common purification.

qpr_core_16.title: The exact history flag and the three unnormalized states $\psi$, $\varphi$, $\gamma$
qpr_core_16.nl: `ExactHistoryFlag` is the central bookkeeping object of the reduction: a seed, the reveal history it determines, and the conditioned answers of both players — exactly the classical information the two players will try to hold in common. For a fixed flag, the Alice-side and Bob-side purification matrices (from the common purification construction) are formed, and their column indices define the lifted local index types on which everything else lives. On the resulting bipartite space the bundle defines three unnormalized vectors: $\psi(x,y)$, conditioned on both players' newly revealed questions; $\varphi(y)$, conditioned on Bob's question only; and $\gamma(x)$, conditioned on Alice's question only. The shapes make the intended use clear: $\gamma$ is preparable by Alice and $\varphi$ by Bob from information each holds alone, while $\psi$ is the state they would jointly like to hold, so the later estimates bound the distances $\|\gamma - \psi\|$ and $\|\varphi - \psi\|$.

qpr_core_17.title: The theorem statement, postselection costs, and the locally sampleable law
qpr_core_17.nl: This large bundle sets out the goal of the development and the budget that pays for it. `HasExponentialBound v` says that $v(n) \le C e^{-cn}$ for some $c, C > 0$, `HasSubexponentialWitness` is the corresponding negation-style property, and `StandardQuantumParallelRepetition G` is the target statement: if $\omega^*(G) < 1$ then $n \mapsto \omega^*(G^n)$ has an exponential bound. The cost bookkeeping is fixed here as well: the postselection mass is the probability that a repeated strategy wins every coordinate of $D$; the conditional failure of a coordinate outside $D$ and its average over those coordinates measure how much is still lost; and with the log cost $\log(1/\Pr[\text{win } D])$ and the answer cost $|D|\log(|A|\,|B|)$, the *martingale rate* is their sum divided by the number of coordinates outside $D$ — the quantity whose smallness for some subset $D$ drives the whole induction. A second strand normalizes the three history states, refines each player's POVM relative to a flag, and pads the local space with a distinguished $\mathrm{PUnit}$ summand so that leftover weight has somewhere to go. A third strand constructs the distribution the players must jointly sample: joint outcomes of $G^n$ paired with a seed, the postselected joint law, its pushforward to a *locally sampleable tuple* (a distinguished remaining coordinate, a history flag and the two new questions), that tuple's law, and the two reference laws $J_A$, $J_B$ in which one player's question is drawn from the prior and the flag from that player's local conditional — together with the local masses and conditionals they are built from. Also present are the loss constants (a universal error ceiling, the total sampling loss, and the rounded lower bound $1 - \varepsilon/2 - \text{loss}$), prefix masks and prefix relative entropies for chain-rule arguments, and the global history register with its vacuum summand.

qpr_core_18.title: State-distance and information bounds, and the reverse view of a seed
qpr_core_18.nl: Three strands. First, the three history states are packaged as honest unit vectors on one common $d$-dimensional bipartite space and lifted along the locally sampleable tuple, and `ExactSourceStateDistanceBound` $\eta$ is the proposition that both $\mathbb{E}\|\gamma - \psi\|^2$ and $\mathbb{E}\|\varphi - \psi\|^2$, averaged over that law, are at most $8\eta$ — the quantum half of the "both players nearly hold the same state" requirement. Second, the classical half: the classical information rate is $\big(3\log(1/\Pr[\text{win }D]) + 2|D|\log(|A||B|)\big)$ divided by the number of remaining coordinates, `ExactSourceClassicalInformationBound` asserts that the relative entropies of the true tuple law with respect to $J_A$ and to $J_B$ are at most that rate, and the accompanying equivalences split a tuple so that each such relative entropy decomposes into a marginal and a conditional part, with $\sqrt{\text{rate}/2}$ recorded as the Pinsker rate. Operator-level entropy increments and variation functionals attached to a flag also live here. Third, the *reverse* view of a seed: a player sees only its own side of the bipartition, and `ExactReverseSideContext` records everything else — the complementary side, a ranking of each side, the other side's cut, and the ignored bit — so that a forward seed can be reconstructed from its side together with a context and a marker. Prefix encode/decode maps for the chain rule complete the bundle.

qpr_core_19.title: Partition fibers of the reverse Alice view
qpr_core_19.nl: Two short declarations continuing the reverse-seed analysis. The first shows that for a fixed side $S$ and a coordinate $i \in S$, the Boolean partitions whose Alice side together with the marked coordinate equals $S$ are in bijection with $\mathrm{Bool}$: the partition is forced away from $i$, and the only remaining freedom is its value at $i$. This is what makes the fibers of the seed-to-side map uniform, and hence lets the conditional seed weights of the following bundles be computed exactly. The second gives the canonical partition realizing a prescribed side in Bob's version of the same correspondence, with the roles of $\mathrm{true}$ and $\mathrm{false}$ interchanged.

qpr_core_20.title: Conditional seed weights and the forward seed law
qpr_core_20.nl: The fiber computation of the previous bundle is repeated for Bob's side, and then used to write down conditional seed weights: for a fixed side $S$, the weight of a seed is its uniform forward weight divided by the total weight of the sides equal to $S$, and is set to zero for seeds whose side differs. Alice's and Bob's versions differ only in which side of the bipartition is held fixed. The bundle closes by packaging the uniform forward weight on `ExactForwardSeed` as a genuine `FiniteEventLaw`, which requires the nonnegativity and normalization facts about that weight; this is the probability space over which the later averages over random bipartitions and orderings are taken.

qpr_core_21.title: Seed-reweighted event laws and the marker encoding of a seed
qpr_core_21.nl: The first group makes the conditional seed weights into event laws and then couples a seed law to a strategy: multiplying a seed weight by the outcome weight of a repeated strategy gives a law on (seed, outcome) pairs, restricting to the event that every coordinate of $D$ is won gives the postselected posterior, and pushing that posterior forward along a projection together with a flag gives the joint laws whose relative entropies define the per-step information increments of a chain rule over a prefix of revealed coordinates. The second group is combinatorial surgery supporting the reverse view: a seed is encoded as a triple (side, side context, marker position) and decoded back, and the auxiliary lemmas convert between a ranking of a set and a ranking of that set with the marked coordinate inserted or deleted, and between a ranking and a permutation. Together with the explicit context weight, these are what let a sum over seeds be re-indexed as a sum over sides and markers without changing total weight.

qpr_core_22.title: Operator entropy potentials for the fair seed, and further stopped-state constructions
qpr_core_22.nl: The bulk of this bundle is the operator-level entropy bookkeeping of the reduction. For a history flag one forms *high* and *low* operator potentials — Born masses of the strategy's state against filters built from the spectral entropy kernel — separately for Alice and Bob and separately in the forward ("fair") and reverse (marker-conditioned) views; their differences are the accepted entropies and the accepted variations, and `ExactFairOperatorEntropyBound` $\eta$ is the proposition that both accepted entropies are at most $2\eta$ times the postselection mass. Supporting definitions describe which coordinates of a question tuple each side has fixed (the question masks and prefixes), the joint prefix question and operator masses and their filters, and the purely scalar counting analogues of the same quantities, used to compare the operator estimate with a classical one. Grouped in by dependency order rather than by theme, the bundle also carries a block of stopped-state constructions belonging to the rounding protocol: flag mismatch and asynchronous flag masses for the multi-copy heterogeneous protocol, the per-copy width bookkeeping, the target-first spectral unitaries for the two players, and several coherent bucket and phase states.

qpr_core_23.title: Rounded samplers, shared flags, and the global POVMs of the rounded strategy
qpr_core_23.nl: Three strands. The classical one rounds the sampler: the reference laws $J_A$ and $J_B$ are replaced by rational approximations over a common denominator, the shared-permutation gadget is applied to both players, and a mismatch functional measures how often their samples disagree; `ExactSourceSharedFlag` is the shared randomness they consume, one permutation per sampler index, and further definitions give the two players' sampled histories, the event that these match, independent product weights and coordinate marginals, and the postselected question laws of each player. The second strand is POVM plumbing: POVMs assembled from blocks indexed by a dependent family, reindexed along an equivalence, two-block and deterministic POVMs, transport across different decidability instances, and finally the padded and *global* Alice and Bob POVMs on the global history register together with its catalyst factor, with the induced winning effect both as a matrix and as a continuous linear map. The third strand continues the reverse-view information analysis: prefix entropy increments and informations in the reverse view, the propositions asserting that a player can identify the conditional history from what it sees, marked history contexts, and the "next step" joint and prior laws of the chain rule. The bundle also carries the tail of the protocol's error accounting, including a public-bucket loss of the form $(10 + 8Q/B)\cdot\text{asynchronous} + \dots$ and the associated prefix hazards.

qpr_core_24.title: One-game rounding: the target proposition and the stopped-branch machinery
qpr_core_24.nl: The conceptual centre of this bundle is a pair of propositions. `ExactSourceSupportPreservingClassicalSampler` asserts the existence of a rational sampler — a denominator, numerators summing to it, support preservation, and closeness in total variation to the true conditionals — for a given base flag and accuracy. `ExactSourceOneGameRounding G` is the key statement the whole apparatus is aimed at: there is a constant $K_0 \ge 0$ such that for every $n$, every strategy for $G^n$, and every subset $D$ with remaining coordinates and positive postselection mass, if the average conditional failure of the remaining coordinates is small then one can build a strategy for a *single* copy of $G$ whose winning probability is at least $1 - \varepsilon/2 - \text{totalSamplingLoss}$. Everything else in the bundle is the operator plumbing that makes such a strategy: conjugation of a POVM by a unitary, entrywise-conjugate vectors and POVMs (to move between a state and its transpose), the catalyst basis equivalences, the selected-copy local index and its cleaned and ideal stages, matched branches, the branch decomposition of a state indexed by a stopping flag with its per-branch and global winning effects, question-dependent local actions, and a long list of index equivalences and reindexing unitaries that let the same stopped state be read either as a tensor product over copies or as one bipartite register.

qpr_core_25.title: The one-scale rounded strategy and the three comparison vectors
qpr_core_25.nl: This bundle assembles the rounded strategy itself. For each copy $j$ of the protocol, the cleaned, selected and flag-controlled stage unitaries act on the retained history register together with its spectral and bucket parts, and each comes with a finite-stage decoder; a family of index equivalences regroups history, phase and work registers so that these local actions can be applied at all. The result is `physical8OneScaleActualSourceFlaggedStrategy` (also exported under an `unconditional` alias): a flagged single-copy strategy for $G$ whose shared state is the prepared stopping state, whose local unitaries depend on the question, and whose measurements are the global padded POVMs of the previous bundle. The `integratorActualC485` group then fixes the objects the analysis compares: on each branch, indexed by a source tuple and a copy index, it defines the *actual* vector the protocol produces, the *canonical* idealized vector, and the *source* vector coming from the original repeated strategy, along with the retained and normalized diagonal work states, the two players' POVMs, and the branch winning-effect operator. These three vectors and that operator are precisely the inputs of the ledger-style estimates stated later.

qpr_core_26.title: Explicit rate constants, trivial strategies, and the rounding context
qpr_core_26.nl: The bundle fixes the explicit constants of the final bound: a universal rate $1/(8(4B)^{12})$, the gap rate $\text{universal} \cdot \varepsilon^{13}/(\varepsilon + \ell)$, a conditioning tolerance $\varepsilon/4$, a catalyst accuracy $(\varepsilon/(16K))^{12}$, and a rounding coefficient assembling the sampling-loss constants; a large numeric constant for the physical rounding is also named. The trivial strategy on a one-dimensional system that always answers a fixed pair $(a,b)$ is defined here as the fallback used when the interesting construction is unavailable. The bundle then gives the flag POVMs and question-dependent stopping unitaries the rounded players actually apply, the targets they aim at, and the Born functionals that evaluate the verifier on a stopped state, both in the selected and the raw physical form. It closes with the bookkeeping records: `...SamplerData` (a base flag plus a rational sampler that is support preserving and accurate to $\gamma$), `...StoppingHazardData` (the protocol parameters $w, N, L, P, Q, m$ with the positivity and fineness side conditions they must satisfy, tied to a hazard parameter $\alpha$), two ledger propositions collecting the analytic inequalities among the actual, canonical and source branch vectors and the verifier operator (mass bounds, deviation, clipping and bad-event budget), and `UnconditionalActualFairSourceRoundingContext`, which bundles all the hypotheses — remaining coordinates, positive postselection mass, small failure rate, sampler data and stopping data — into a single record.

qpr_core_27.title: Derived fields of a rounding context
qpr_core_27.nl: These declarations are the accessors of the rounding-context record, so that the analytic statements can be phrased in terms of a single context variable $c$ rather than a dozen separate hypotheses. First, a constructor building a context from the positivity hypotheses and the sampler and stopping data. Then the derived data: the ambient dimension $d$ as the cardinality of the global history index, the constant width and schedule functions of the single-scale protocol, the source index type (the locally sampleable tuples) together with its law, the three unit vectors $\gamma$, $\varphi$, $\psi$ attached to a source index, the branch space attached to a pair (source index, copy index), and the *actual* branch vector the protocol produces there. Nothing new is asserted here; the content is purely the naming of the fields the later estimates quantify over.

qpr_core_28.title: The rounded strategy extracted from a rounding context
qpr_core_28.nl: The accessors continue and end in the object the argument is after. Alongside the actual vector come the canonical and source branch vectors, default answers chosen from the nonemptiness of the answer alphabets, and the branch winning-effect operator. Three error budgets are then named: the *deviation* is the law-averaged squared distance $\sum_h \mathrm{law}(h) \sum_j \|\text{actual} - \text{canonical}\|^2$, the *clipping* is the clip energy of the construction, and the *bad* budget is $64\sqrt{\text{martingaleRate}} + \alpha^{1/3} + \alpha^{2/3}$, so that all three vanish as the martingale rate and the hazard parameter go to zero. The remaining fields name the shared flag and fiber types, the two players' flag POVMs, their question-dependent stopping unitaries, the prepared shared state, and finally `rounded`, the flagged single-copy strategy for $G$ built from all of this — the strategy whose winning probability the one-game rounding statement lower-bounds.
